title: Doughnut
logline: The spare tire, months before it matters. A strip about a tire.

panels.composition: Gully's lot, Tuesday. The Legacy up on a jack. GULLY holding a shredded tire. WOOD holding the dog.

balloons.text: Rear left's gone. You've got the doughnut.
The little one. Fifty miles, fifty miles an hour. Don't go anywhere.

image.prompt: an old Subaru wagon up on a jack in a gravel lot, a stocky man holding a shredded tire, a thin man holding an old dog, clean ink

panels.composition: The doughnut spare, absurdly small, going on.

image.prompt: close-up of a comically small spare tire being fitted to an old car's wheel hub
a thin man looking down doubtfully at a tiny spare tire on his car

panels.composition: The Legacy driving off on three real tires and one toy, the car listing slightly, the dog's head out the window, the blue haze. Gully watching, shaking his head.

image.prompt: an old Subaru wagon driving away on three full tires and one tiny spare so that it lists slightly, an old dog's head out the window, a stocky man watching and shaking his head, no words
image.notes: 'Don't go anywhere.' He drives to the San Juans on it nine months later.

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The doughnut. Fifty miles. He'll take it four hundred.
